# rind on pi5-nofan-1p5ghz: Raspberry Pi 5 (Cortex-A76, no fan, held at 1.5 GHz)

Five rounds on a Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0 (BCM2712, four Cortex-A76 cores, no fan, the clock held at 1.5 GHz) at [kixel-ai/rind `a6577cb4`](https://github.com/kixel-ai/rind/commit/a6577cb4a4b48af06385f8d748f3892c07cc229e), on 2026-11-13 from 11:47 AM to 3:26 PM America/Los_Angeles (the board clock is on the same zone).

The binaries were the rind-bench criterion harnesses, cross-compiled for `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`. This set was not produced by `admin/bench-report run`. Each published time is the median of the five rounds' criterion estimates (`pi5-nofan-1p5ghz.json`, schema 1, each run's estimate in `runs_ns`). [RUNS.md](RUNS.md) lists every run, [facts.txt](facts.txt) the hardware, and [NOTES.md](NOTES.md) how the board was run.

**All times are at 1.5 GHz.** They are not comparable with a Pi 5 at its rated 2.4 GHz. Ratios between libraries are what carry over.

- Board: Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0, 8 GB, no fan
- CPU: Cortex-A76, aarch64, 4 logical CPUs, held at 1.5 GHz by a boot-time thermal-cap service (min = max), governor `performance` during the rounds
- OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) (Linux 6.18.60+rpt-rpi-2712)
- Toolchain: rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01), cargo 1.98.1; cross-built on macOS with clang 22, rust-lld and a Pi 5 sysroot
- OpenSSL linked: OpenSSL 3.5.7 9 Jun 2026 (the Pi's system library; built against 3.5.9 headers)
- Libraries: rind, aws-lc-rs, ring, RustCrypto, graviola, libcrux, OpenSSL
- CPU features rind reads (rind-cpuid): aes, neon, pmull, sha2; absent: dit, sha3. No library was refused.
- Criterion: `--noplot --warm-up-time 1 --measurement-time 3 --sample-size 10`
- Pin: cpu3. No run was flagged noisy (other busy CPUs 0.00–0.01 of a 1.0 limit).
- Thermal: 48.8–75.2 °C during the timed rounds, clock 1.5 GHz in every sample, no live throttle bits (see NOTES.md for the sticky bits)
- `build_cost`: not measured (the binaries were cross-compiled on another host)

## Method and validation

Validation ran on the board before the rounds, from test binaries cross-built at the same rind commit, following CI's aarch64 host tests and its "Artificial CPU feature tests (aarch64)": 174 test binaries, 0 failed, every binary exited 0. Two CPU tiers: the board's crypto extensions in use (`RIND_TEST_ARM_CRYPTO_EXT=1`; the A76 has no SHA-3 extension) and denied (`RIND_CPU_DISABLE_aes`, `_pmull`, `_sha2`).

| Tier | Binaries | Passed | Failed | Ignored |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tests, crypto extensions in use | 52 | 1239 | 0 | 32 |
| tests, crypto extensions denied | 52 | 1239 | 0 | 32 |
| memory-wipe tests, in use | 2 | 28 | 0 | 0 |
| memory-wipe tests, denied | 2 | 28 | 0 | 0 |
| debug, default features | 52 | 1239 | 0 | 32 |
| debug, no default features | 9 | 791 | 0 | 32 |
| debug, wipe-zeroing | 3 | 26 | 0 | 0 |
| slow CCTV vectors + `detects_the_expected_cpu`, in use | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| slow CCTV vectors + `detects_the_expected_cpu`, denied | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

Doctests were not run (the tests were cross-compiled).

| `x25519-ecdh`, `p256-ecdh`, `ed25519-sign`, `ed25519-verify`, `p384-ecdh`, `p521-ecdh` | 2.32× aws-lc-rs; 1.54× aws-lc-rs; 1.46× aws-lc-rs; 1.44× aws-lc-rs; 1.64× aws-lc-rs; 1.66× aws-lc-rs | On aarch64, rind a6577cb4 runs s2n-bignum's _alt (wide-multiplier) schedules, which suit cores with fast high multiplies; the Cortex-A76 is not one. aws-lc-rs picks its schedule per core. The narrow-multiplier A/B on a Pi 5 at the same 1.5 GHz cap (hosts/pi5/ab-narrow-mul/) closes these to 0.93-0.99x of aws-lc-rs with the narrow schedules (steelhead99x/rind PR #33), which are not in a6577cb4. |
